thread:
Jules: Heads-up 0 mins before standup my downstairs neighbor decided it was the perfect time to vacuum. laptop mic is a massacre. anyone have guerrilla soundproofing tips for 1-2 hour calls? :weary:
Priya: rugs + curtains are incredible. if you can't get those, try moving to a different room with more soft surfaces. hiding the laptop on a cushion helps damp vibrations. :rug:
Omar: cheap mic trick: use a roll of fleece around the mic or a DIY isolation shield made from a cereal box and some acoustic foam (or towels). also try noise suppression like Krisp or built-in Zoom.
Nina: I actually use a baking cooling rack + thick scarf rig to prop a blanket behind my laptop (looks ridiculous but cuts reflections). if you're desperate, call from your bathroom 609 (tiles are weird but small room helps).
Jules: bathroom calls are wild. tempted. anyone made a "mini shield" that doesn't look like a science project?
Priya: small metal coat hanger bent into a semicircle, cover with felt and attach with clothespins. cheap and semi-professional.
Omar: also, lower your laptop mic input gain and enable echo cancellation. if you have an old headset, the mic on that will be way better than your laptop's built-in one.
ops-bot: reminder: housekeeping 6ae scheduled building maintenance 10:4511:00 local, expect intermittent hallway noise.
Nina: haha ops-bot perfectly timed. Jules, if you do the coat-hanger trick, post a pic. DIY content fuels the channel. :popcorn:
Jules: will attempt the hanger + scarf solution tonight and report back. if it's a disaster, i'll include the bathroom-stand remote-call alternative photo. :camera_with_flash:
